transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-26
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Thalassa CTO), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Ravi Desai (Security), Jules Kim (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for Thalassa marketplace joint solution. Covered packaging, connectivity (VPC), KMS/HSM integration, quantization and perf/price tradeoffs, and lab validation plan. Agreed on next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. we'll just do quick intros, then go into packaging + the VPC/KMS bits. Ethan will run the tech demo portion.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Hi all, Maya here. happy to be on. we are under a tight timeline — legal wants listing ready for procurement review by late June if possible.
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: Liam, platform — mainly focused on networking and CI/CD for the connector. we currently run K8s on-prem and in aws us-east, looking at hybrid listing.
[00:32] Ethan Chu: Great. small clarifier: when you say "listing" are you looking to have a managed pre-packaged connector on the marketplace or an on-prem helm chart with a marketplace billing integration?
[00:44] Jules Kim: Ideally both — buyer can choose hosted Redwood (hosted API) or deploy our joint offering via marketplace with a private connector. The primary ask is clear install/upgrade path.
[00:56] Sofia Martinez: Understood. Today's agenda: packaging checklist, VPC peering/VPN and KMS, quantization/perf tradeoffs for Thalassa models, and lab validation steps.
[01:10] Ethan Chu: I'll share my screen — starting with the helm chart layout. The repo we usually hand off has three pieces: helm chart + values schema, minimal operator hooks for credential rotation, and a packaging script that builds the marketplace artifact.
[01:28] Maya Patel: Are those operator hooks required? we try to avoid operators if possible.
[01:34] Ethan Chu: They're optional — for customers who want automatic rotation and zero-downtime key swaps we recommend them. For simple installs we provide a one-shot job that fetches secrets from their KMS.
[01:45] Liam O'Connor: On the KMS front, we use AWS KMS for cloud and Thales for on-prem HSMs. Do you support a mixed KMS flow?
[01:56] Ethan Chu: Yes, Redwood Private supports a KMS abstraction layer — you can point to AWS KMS or an external HSM via KMIP. small caveat: audit logs are surfaced differently depending on provider — we map events but field names sometimes change.
[02:12] Ravi Desai: We need to verify FIPS and key attestation for the HSM. Also need to see SOC 2 artifacts before we proceed.
[02:20] Sofia Martinez: We can share the SOC 2 summary and the standard redwood security pack link after the call. for attestation we usually run a security checklist with an SE and our compliance lead.
[02:32] Maya Patel: Cool. can we talk about traffic profile? i'll give a high level: most of our inference is ~250 tokens per request, 95th latency SLO is 150ms per request for hosted, but on the private marketplace offering buyers are okay with slightly higher latency if cost reduces.
[02:52] Ethan Chu: That's helpful. For 250 token requests latency targets, we usually recommend 8-bit quantized variants on p4d or a dedicated lower-cost gpu pool depending on throughput. There's a tradeoff: quantization reduces memory and cost but can increase small inaccuracy in certain models.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: Do you have telemetry we can run to validate quality regressions per prompt set?
[03:16] Ethan Chu: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes eval harnesses and a prompt-based regression alerting system. we'll share a light-weight eval job you can run in your lab. it spits out per-prompt QA deltas and per-token cost estimates.
[03:30] Sofia Martinez: we'll attach that to the lab run so you can verify no quality regressions before listing.
[03:36] Maya Patel: About billing — marketplace billing has to support metering of tokens plus optional reserved capacity. how do you propose we map that?
[03:45] Ethan Chu: Two options: a) marketplace SKU that bills per-token via Redwood hosted API with back-to-back SKUs to Thalassa for revenue share, or b) marketplace listing that deploys to customer infra and uses an onboarded meter that reports usage back to Redwood billing agent. both have tradeoffs for latency and data residency.
[04:03] Jules Kim: Option b is preferred for our enterprise buyers due to data residency.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: For option b — is there a lightweight meter we can run as a sidecar? we want something that doesn't add much latency.
[04:17] Ethan Chu: Yes, we provide a telemetry sidecar that aggregates token counts and sends batched metrics to a billing endpoint. it's buffered and can be run asynchronously to avoid per-request latency hits. the sidecar also exports prometheus metrics for your observability stack.
[04:33] Maya Patel: Great. any certification requirements for marketplace listing?
[04:37] Sofia Martinez: The marketplace requires a packaging checksum, signed artifact, and a minimal onboarding doc. For hybrid/onprem we also need a network connectivity diagram and a runbook for upgrading. we'll provide the packaging checklist in the next-day follow-up.
[04:53] Ethan Chu: Now the VPC connectivity patterns: there are three common topologies — VPC peering, PrivateLink-style interface endpoints, and VPN tunnel. For on-prem hybrid, we recommend PrivateLink where possible. For buyers behind strict egress controls, we support a connector with an outbound-only proxy.
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: We prefer PrivateLink but our infra team is worried about cross-account VPC peering policy. will there be a dedicated sub-account per customer?
[05:22] Sofia Martinez: For marketplace deployments you can choose a listing model that provisions a managed account per customer or a BYO option. This is part of the packaging options.
[05:31] Maya Patel: What about upgrades — can we do canary deploys? we need zero downtime.
[05:36] Ethan Chu: Yes, the chart supports canary rollouts and canary traffic steering via a built-in rollout controller. That controller talks to Redwood Console for feature flags and fallback policies. Caveat: the controller is a small controller so if you can't run operators, you can emulate canary via staged helm upgrades and health checks.
[05:58] Jules Kim: Quick question on model variants — buyers may want to switch between quantized and fp16 variants dynamically for burst traffic. How does that work?
[06:07] Ethan Chu: We support routing by policy — pulses can route to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical requests and route to fp16 when quality SLO is exceeded. The KV cache is shared across variants when compatible, but there are cases where cache invalidation is required (for different tokenizer states).
[06:29] Liam O'Connor: Who handles OS/binary compatibility for the onprem bundle? we need to know supported distros and libc versions.
[06:36] Ethan Chu: Our packaging targets Ubuntu 22.04 and RHEL 8+ in the helm chart; we also publish a container with musl compatibility for edge, but that variant has limited GPU vendor drivers. We'll add a compatibility matrix to the repo.
[06:52] Sofia Martinez: I'll pause — quick poll: any blockers that would prevent June listing deadline?
[06:58] Maya Patel: Main blockers: SOC2 doc review, KMS attestation, and time for lab validation. If we get those sorted in two weeks it's feasible.
[07:08] Ravi Desai: Also need legal to sign marketplace terms; we'll need sample contract language.
[07:14] Sofia Martinez: Noted — we'll connect legal separately.
[07:18] Ethan Chu: Demo time — showing a short run of the helm install and telemetry. (screen share noises)
[07:30] [screenshare] Ethan Chu: Here is the values.yaml we recommend. Note the sections: credentials.kms, networking.privateLink, metrics.sidecar.enabled. we default to async batching for metering to keep p95 under SLO.
[07:49] Liam O'Connor: Small nit: values.yaml uses field name 'kmsProvider' but our infra expects 'kms_provider' — can you make aliasing?
[07:58] Ethan Chu: we can add a mapping layer, yes — the helm chart includes a migration hook that normalizes fields for common CI systems.
[08:12] Maya Patel: Can we see the size of the runtime container? members on my team worry about air-gapped downloads.
[08:18] Ethan Chu: The base runtime container for the quantized variant is about 1.2GB compressed; fp16 is 4.6GB. For air-gapped installs we supply a downloadable tarball and a small bootstrap that verifies checksums.
[08:34] Sofia Martinez: moving on — lab validation plan. propose 2h lab with two phases: 1) install + smoke test (30-45m), 2) workload sweep with telemetry and quality regression (75-90m). We'd like Thalassa to provide 3 representative prompt sets.
[08:54] Liam O'Connor: we'll provide those traces; how do we share?
[08:58] Ethan Chu: upload to the gs:// link i put in the notes or S3 share. We'll provide a small harness script to replay traces with configurable QPS and token length distribution.
[09:09] Jules Kim: For evaluation, can we integrate our internal QA rubric? we track hallucination on certain categories.
[09:15] Ethan Chu: absolutely — the eval harness supports custom metrics; we can map your rubric to our alert thresholds.
[09:22] Maya Patel: Security follow-up: Ravi will need to validate that the telemetry sidecar doesn't exfiltrate PII. can we do an audit?
[09:30] Ethan Chu: yes, the sidecar only aggregates token counts and hashes for provenance; payloads are not sent. we can provide a detailed data flow diagram and sample logs.
[09:41] Ravi Desai: please include the retention policy — will logs be retained in Redwood?
[09:46] Sofia Martinez: retention is configurable per-customer; by default hosted traces are kept 30 days but for Private deployments we ship with 0 retention and customers control storage. we'll include that in the security pack.
[09:58] Maya Patel: Any thoughts on performance tuning during storm events?
[10:02] Ethan Chu: autoscaling policies can be set to scale up by queued tokens and latency signals; we also offer burst credits via dedicated reserved pools if you want guaranteed headroom.
[10:15] Liam O'Connor: For the marketplace listing metadata — what fields do we need to provide?
[10:20] Sofia Martinez: Title, short description, icons, certs (SOC2 summary), packaging checksum, install runbook, and networking diagram. We'll provide a template.
[10:31] Maya Patel: Regarding revenue split and billing granularity, we'll loop in partnerships. preferrably per-token with reserved capacity option.
[10:38] Sofia Martinez: noted. we'll coordinate with partnerships to draft the SKU model.
[10:43] Ethan Chu: Quick technical caveat: if you want onprem quantization support on older GPUs, kernels may not be optimized and latency might be higher; we can compile a fallback kernel but it increases build complexity.
[10:58] Liam O'Connor: acceptable as long as it's documented.
[11:02] Jules Kim: Anything else on the roadmap we should surface?
[11:06] Sofia Martinez: Rollout: share packaging assets (Ethan), customer traces (Liam), security review (Ravi). target lab run week of 2027-06-07 and marketplace listing readiness by 2027-06-23 for procurement review.
[11:20] Maya Patel: That works. can we schedule the SOC/compliance call next week?
[11:25] Ravi Desai: yes, prefer Tuesday 14:00 local.
[11:28] Sofia Martinez: I'll send calendar invites.
[11:31] Ethan Chu: One last demo note — we default to enabling prefix/KV caching. if your model uses dynamic prompts with lots of context switching that can increase cache misses. suggest we run a cache-hit analysis during lab.
[11:47] Liam O'Connor: we'll include that in traces.
[11:51] Sofia Martinez: Great. quick recap of next steps and then we'll close.
[11:56] Sofia Martinez: Recap: Ethan share helm + packaging checklist; Liam upload traces; Ravi security artifacts; Sofia to schedule lab and compliance call; all agree targets.
[12:08] Maya Patel: thanks everyone. excited to move fast.
[12:12] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all — we'll follow up with links and a calendar.
[12:15] Call ended.

Notes about transcription: occasional name misspellings and timestamps approximate. Some technical terms auto-corrected by STT (e.g., 'PrivateLink' got transcribed as 'private link') but content reviewed by AE post-call.
